entries.answer: Palayag is the general word for a command or an instruction, and it is a Cebuano compound built from the verb payag, which is also what the English phrase comes from in the older sense of obeying. It is used for both a direct order and a gentler request, and the difference between the two is carried by the affix on the verb rather than by the word itself, so the same palayag can be a command or an instruction depending on how the rest of the sentence is built. In a classroom or workplace context it is the normal word for a direction, and it is also what you use telling someone to do something simple, such as palayag og pagsulat, meaning start writing. A learner who uses the same tone for everything will sound blunt or apologetic by accident, and the practical fix is to vary the affix rather than to look for a different noun, since there is not a separate word for the polite version.
